stories.title: Six dead after passenger ship carrying 267 people sinks off coast of northern Cyprus
stories.summary: Video footage circulating on social media appears to show passengers in life jackets sitting on the overturned ship as they wait to be reached. Six people have reportedly died after a passenger ship capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday. The vessel, which was reportedly sailing from Kyreneia in Cyprus to the Turkish port of Taşucu, sank at around midday. Turkey's Interior Ministry said 259 passengers and eight crew members were on board the vessel when it began taking on water roughly 6 km off the coast of Kyreneia. Murat Senkul, the mayor of Kyreneia, described the situation as "very serious" in a post on Facebook, adding that a rescue operation was under way. Ünal Üstel, the prime minister of northern Cyprus, said 172 people have been rescued so far, CNN Turk reported. The cause of the incident is not yet clear. Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides' office said in statement on the sinking: “Our position is clear: when human lives are at risk, we contribute with every available means." "The Republic of Cyprus has the resources, the operational capacity, and, above all, the readiness to provide immediate assistance," it added. Check back for further details.

stories.title: Fate of 99 people on board the vessel remains unknown — Kyrenia mayor
stories.summary: Mayor Murat Shenkul stated that Turkish Cypriot authorities have so far managed to contact 159 of the 258 people who were on board
article_sentences: The fate of the 99 people aboard the ship that ran into trouble off the coast of Kyrenia remains unknown, Mayor Murat Shenkul told the Kibris newspaper.
The mayor stated that Turkish Cypriot authorities have so far managed to contact 159 of the 258 people who were on board.
The ship’s crew is among those unaccounted for.
Earlier, Kibris reported that a high-speed vessel carrying approximately 270 passengers and crew members was in distress off the coast of northern Cyprus.
According to the newspaper, the incident occurred 6.6 kilometers off the coast near Kyrenia.
The cruise ship began taking on water for an unknown reason, and preliminary estimates suggest that it had approximately 270 passengers and crew members on board.
Numerous vessels were subsequently dispatched to the area to provide assistance.

stories.title: French high schools scramble to work out rules as phone ban takes effect
stories.summary: The new school year starts on Tuesday in France, and with it comes a new rule: mobile phones will no longer be allowed in high schools. The ban came into force a week before the first day of term, leaving schools with little time to work out how to put it into practice.

stories.title: 13-year-old among 321 arrested as Hong Kong police seize drugs worth HK$130m
stories.summary: Hong Kong police have arrested 321 people, including a 13-year-old, and seized HK$130 million (US$16.5 million) worth of suspected illegal drugs during a seven-week citywide crackdown. Code-named “Tailbacker”, the operation ran from July 12 to August 29, and uncovered 234 drug-related cases, police said on Sunday.
